title: PR #313 · panel apply
blurb: The other half of #313: the woodwork slice of applySettings, and the fifth ApplyReport category it earned. The other four are all transitions, and a transition cannot describe a configuration that was wrong from the first frame — so `resolved` states rather than diffs, on every apply, whether or not anything moved.

presets.name: pick sapele in the panel
presets.blurb: rebuild-class: the menu moved, the bookcase has not, and the read-back names both

presets.name: nothing moved
presets.blurb: the argument for the fifth category — four empty transition lists, and the sheet still says what it is running

steps.note: Five report lists. applied / needsRebuild / needsReload / refused are transitions; resolved is a statement.

steps.label: fibre
steps.note: laid by the sheet the shelf was BUILT with, not by the module's default constant

steps.label: fibreNo
steps.name: refused
steps.expr: refused.concat('wood fibre: there is no canvas to draw it on, so the woodwork stays smooth')

steps.label: holdFibre
steps.name: fibreInForce
steps.note: not applied and not asked for — but still reported, so a fibre that never bound says so on every apply after the one that discovered it

steps.label: readback
steps.note: resolved from `next`, NOT read off woodwork.resolved — the two differ exactly when a species change is waiting for a rebuild, and a typo has to reach the report when the value is set rather than one rebuild later

steps.expr: ({ applied, needsRebuild, refused: refused.concat(readBack.refused), resolved: readBack.resolved })

steps.note: Compared AFTER resolution, never as raw strings: everything off-roster resolves to the default, so walnut and rosewood name one shelf. Comparing the requests would offer a rebuild for a change a rebuild cannot make.

steps.label: off
steps.expr: ({ species: $env.default, sheet: $env.sheets[$env.default], lay: $env.sheets[$env.default], refused: 'woodwork sheet: "' + requested + '" is not a sheet anybody has rendered, so the woodwork is showing ' + $env.default + '. The roster is ' + $env.roster.join(', ') })
({ species, sheet, lay: sheet ?? $env.sheets[$env.default], refused: null })

steps.note: Pure, and in a module with no Three.js in it, so G54 can assert on it without a WebGL context.

steps.name: sheet
steps.expr: wanted.sheet === null ? 'no map — the mean-matched flat twin' : wanted.sheet.url + ', laid at ' + wanted.lay.unitsPerTile + ' world units'

steps.name: waiting
steps.expr: wanted.species === built ? '' : ' — built with ' + built + ', rebuild to change it'

steps.name: lines
steps.expr: ['woodwork sheet: ' + wanted.species + ' (' + sheet + ')' + waiting, 'wood fibre: ' + fibreInForce + (fibreInForce === fibreAsked ? '' : ' (asked for ' + fibreAsked + ')')]
steps.note: G54's first draft matched the species by bare substring and was green on a read-back naming no species at all — rosewood and sapele each appear inside their own URL. Anchoring to `woodwork sheet: <name> (` reddened six clauses.
refused AND reported, never silently defaulted

steps.label: nocanvas
steps.note: no 2D context — the caller reports refused, never silently smooth
